transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not taking up your time with something silly, because I'm sure it's really nothing major. But, well, my doctor suggested I come in because I've just been feeling a little... wound up, I guess? Almost all day. 

It's just this strange feeling like my body is always bracing for something, even when I’m just sitting at my computer for work, or trying to relax after dinner. I don't know if that makes sense? I just wasn't sure if that was normal, or if that's the right kind of thing to be coming in here for...
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things in your life, like work, family, or other everyday issues?

Um, well... I suppose everyone worries a little bit, right? I try really hard not to make a fuss, but... yes, I guess my mind does sort of jump from one concern to another. 

It's really just normal things, though. Like, I'll be thinking about my sister down in Arecibo, and then suddenly I'm fretting about whether I missed an email at the office. Or I'll start thinking about my husband driving home in traffic, or making sure I have everything ready for my church commitments, or the bills... just silly little everyday things. 

I just like to be responsible, you know? But I do find myself... well, preparing for problems that haven’t even happened yet. Is that... is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope I'm answering your question okay.
Have you noticed feeling unusually tired or lacking energy, even if you haven’t done anything physically or mentally exhausting?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I do get a little tired by the end of the day, but I'm looking at a computer screen for hours for my job, so I figure that's pretty normal for someone my age, right? 

I try really hard to keep my energy up and stay on top of things. I definitely haven't noticed feeling exhausted for no reason, at least. I hope it's okay that I don't have that one... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Am I being helpful?
Do you ever feel like you can't control or stop the worrying, even when you try?

Um, well... I do try really hard to just push it out of my mind. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around dwelling on things on purpose! But... yes, I suppose sometimes it is a little hard to stop it once it starts. 

Like, I’ll be at my desk and I’ll tell myself, ‘Daniela, enough, just focus on this report,’ but... I don't know, one small thought just sort of turns into five more. And then, before I even realize it, I’ve spent half an hour checking my messages or just replaying all the little things that could go wrong. 

I always get my work done, though! I promise I'm very diligent. I just... I wish I could turn the thoughts off a little easier when I need to. Is that the sort of thing you're asking about? I really hope I'm making sense.
Do you ever find yourself fidgeting, pacing, or feeling physically restless, like you can't sit still even if you want to?

Um, well... I don't really pace around or anything like that. I'm usually very good at staying at my desk. But... I suppose I do feel a little... tight? 

I actually think that's sort of why I decided to come in. I just feel kind of wound up most of the day. It's almost like my body is... bracing for something to happen? Even when I'm just sitting at my computer working, or when I'm sitting on the couch trying to relax after dinner. 

I try my best to just stretch it out and not make a big deal of it, but it's just this constant feeling of being tense. I hope that's not too strange... does that count as being restless? I just want to make sure I'm answering you correctly.
Do you ever notice symptoms like your heart racing, sweating more than usual, or shaking or trembling when you're feeling especially anxious or worried?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, maybe occasionally if I'm running late for a meeting or something, my heart might beat a little faster, but that's normal, right? 

I definitely don't sit around shaking or sweating or anything like that. I really try to keep myself composed, especially at work. I wouldn't want anyone to think I couldn't handle my job. So, no, nothing like that. I hope that's okay? I just don't want to make things sound worse than they actually are. Am I giving you the right kind of answers?
Do you ever have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep because your mind is racing with worries, even when you're tired?

Um, well... I do usually fall asleep eventually. I try very hard to practice good sleep hygiene, you know? I don't want to be one of those people who just lies there staring at the ceiling for hours. 

But... I suppose sometimes staying asleep is a little bit of a challenge. I might wake up around three or four in the morning, and my mind just sort of... drifts. I'll start thinking about my sister's next doctor's appointment, or maybe some server issue we're dealing with at work. It's nothing I can't handle, of course! Just... little things. 

And then, even if I do manage to get enough hours of sleep on paper, I sometimes start the morning feeling like I never really rested at all. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm complaining too much. Is that the kind of sleep trouble you mean? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you ever notice muscle tension, like your shoulders or neck feeling very tight, or other physical symptoms when you're feeling anxious or worried?

Um... well, like I mentioned earlier, I do get that sort of... tight feeling? But I wouldn't call it anything major. I mean, my neck and shoulders might get a little stiff sometimes, but honestly, I sit at a computer all day for work. It's probably just from my posture, right? 

I definitely don't have any severe muscle spasms or anything that would require, you know, special treatment. I try to do some light stretching in the evenings so I'm not a bother to anyone about it. I just... I don't want to make it sound like I'm falling apart or anything. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to be helpful.
Have these feelings of tension and worry been causing you a lot of distress or making it hard for you to function normally in your daily life, like at work or with your family?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say a lot of distress! I'm definitely still functioning just fine. I make sure I'm still getting all my work done, and I'm showing up for my family and for church just like always. I really pride myself on being reliable, you know? I'd hate for anyone to think I was dropping the ball. 

But... well, I guess if I'm being completely honest, it might take me a little bit longer to finish my reports at work lately. I just find myself double-checking things a bit more than I used to. Which is just being thorough, right? It's good to be careful. 

And... um, I suppose I have had to apologize a couple of times recently for sounding a little short with the people I care about. I always feel just awful about it afterward, because I really try to be pleasant with everyone. Is... is that the kind of thing you're asking about? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible person to be around. I'm really trying my best to keep everything running smoothly.
Have these feelings of tension and worry been happening most days, and have they been going on for several months now?

Um, well... I suppose it has been most days, yes. But mostly just in the background, you know? Nothing I can't push through. As for how long... oh, let me think. I guess it's been about thirteen months now? 

Yes, right around then. That's when my sister down in Arecibo started needing a lot more help from the family. So it's completely natural to be a little preoccupied with that, right? I mean, anyone would be a bit on edge trying to help coordinate things while still working full-time. I just... I really hope I'm not making a big deal out of normal family responsibilities. I'm just trying to be a supportive sister. Does that timeframe sound like what you were looking for? I want to make sure I'm answering your questions correctly.
Have you noticed any trouble focusing or concentrating on tasks, like your work or reading something, because your mind keeps drifting to worries?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I have trouble focusing. I mean, like I said, I might double-check things at work just to be thorough, but my mind isn't... drifting off or anything like that. I'm still very dedicated to my job. 

I can sit down and read or get through my tasks just fine. I suppose sometimes I might pause for a moment to think about my sister, but that's just normal concern, right? It certainly doesn't stop me from getting my work done. I always make sure to meet my deadlines. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just want to reassure you that I'm keeping up with everything I need to do.
